output.name: Halan

anatomy.part: mast head, the top of the ferry's sail-spar
mast foot on the deck of the hull
belly of the sail, where the canvas bulges
clew, the lower corner of the sail that catches the wind
far lantern at the end of the stay, the boat still out on the sound
pennant tip flying from the masthead

output.myth: Halan is raised for the first crossing of spring, when the ice has gone out of the sound and the boat is loaded with goats, salt and new cloth. Ennu sewed the first one square, so it would carry more and tear less. But a sail is only as good as the hand that ties it. The ferryman ties Halan low over the water, close to the spray, and he does not let it climb. Tall sails catch Tavo's eye. The Gale comes down laughing to take a proud sail off the road and carry it over the cliffs. Nobody has ever bargained with him, so nobody tries. The sail flies until the keel touches stone on the far side. Then it is folded, and hung up in the Lamp Road, where Hesk keeps count. The little lantern on the stay is a boat still out. Aun flew too high once. Sil is still looking for him.
output.verse:
Low over the sound,
the sail holds its breath till stone,
Hesk counts the crossing.
